notes: Counts are first-pass (draft) sentences, c01-c85 (sections, FAQ answers, keyFact values). Added/replacement sentences are listed as a01-a10. Several summaries blended pages; Asthma + Lung UK claims (reliever frequency, NICE 'no blue reliever only') were attributed to the reliever-inhalers page within a blended summary. EXISTING PAGE ENTRY: (1) overview 'about one child in ten and one adult in twelve' not retrieved/supported. (2) seekCare 'peak flow below a third of best' is a test cut-off not supported by retrieved text (retrieved signs: struggling to speak without pausing, reliever not helping, breathlessness stopping speech/eating/sleeping, gasping/choking; blue lips only from unnamed NHS pages). (3) causes 'Genetic susceptibility plus environmental exposure ... early viral infections ... occupational chemicals' not supported: NHS says it is not fully understood what causes asthma; retrieved NHS risk factors are family history of asthma/atopic conditions, bronchiolitis in childhood, childhood tobacco smoke, mother smoking in pregnancy, prematurity/low birth weight. (4) riskFactors 'Eczema and hay fever' and 'Obesity' not in the retrieved NHS list. (5) signs 'A silent chest' and 'Fast breathing, use of accessory muscles' not retrieved. (6) complications 'Airway remodelling and fixed narrowing' not retrieved (steroid-tablet side effects incl. osteoporosis are supported). (7) tests (pulse-oximetry, complete-blood-count) and imaging (x-ray) not supported by retrieved text; NHS lists FeNO, spirometry, peak flow; NG245 adds blood eosinophils/allergy tests. (8) treatment 'long-acting bronchodilator as needed' and 'Attacks are treated with high-dose reliever, oral steroids and oxygen' only partly seen (NHS hospital treatment: oxygen by mask, nebuliser, steroid tablets or injections). (9) related 'pneumonia' not supported. (10) references: 'Global Initiative for Asthma' not retrieved. Draft errors removed: lower life expectancy, COPD overlap, pneumonia from steroids, 'pathway does not cover under 5', spirometry-over-peak-flow preference, pale/grey lips attributed to NHS inform, 'most people prescribed two inhalers'. Dropped severe-asthma phenotype sentences (only research papers retrieved). The NHS asthma page excerpts came through blended summaries; no direct page fetch.
